article_title: Promoting the transition to quantum thinking: development of a secondary school course for addressing knowledge revision, organization, and epistemological challenges
citation: Zuccarini, G., & Michelini, M. (2024). Promoting the transition to quantum thinking: development of a secondary school course for addressing knowledge revision, organization, and epistemological challenges. https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00239
title: JQM open-ended environment for computer-simulated experiments on photon polarization
description: JQM is an "open-ended environment for computer-simulated experiments on photon polarization" whose iconic language depicts idealized physical situations involving single photons. Photons are visualized by their polarization property as segments, not vectors, with devices such as single photon sources, polarizing filters, calcite crystals, screens and counters. It supports theoretical epistemic practices such as thought experiments and interpretation of classical polarization laws in terms of photons.
requirements: Students are informed that segment representations are not real physical representations of photons but supports for theoretical reasoning
target_learners: secondary school students learning quantum mechanics
target_learning_goals: run thought experiments on quantum measurement
examples: The environment represents a photon source with predetermined polarization, filters at arbitrary axes, birefringent crystals, and photon counters
key_sources: Zuccarini, G., & Michelini, M. (2024). Promoting the transition to quantum thinking: development of a secondary school course for addressing knowledge revision, organization, and epistemological challenges. https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00239
